title: Pre-solve checks for a Budget Lock scenario

blocks.text: Budget Lock week at the practice utility (a fictional one): finance and the board send a scenario that changes the snapshot's numbers before the run. A scenario may lock a year's `budget`, cut `crews` (by program and year), `force_in` projects, `fix_start` a project to one year, and `force_out` projects. Before any solve, CIPT Lite runs pre-solve checks that each read **one** project, group or region against **one** limit, so a typed number is caught with its own name instead of a bare `INFEASIBLE` (lesson 9.1.2).

Every check must be **sound**: it fires only when no plan can exist, so a scenario that has a plan never gets a finding. A check compares the least a required project must take with the most a limit can give.

Write, in `checks.py`, `required(snapshot, scenario)`: each must-do and each forced project with its window's start years, and each fixed project with only its fixed year. `required` keeps them all: a required project that is also forced out keeps its window, and a fixed year outside the window is kept as given, because those are exactly the cases `checks` must report as `no-start`. Then `checks(snapshot, scenario)`, which returns a list of `(rule, subject)` findings, in this order:

rows: a required project is forced out, or its fixed year is outside its window (then skip its other checks)
no start left to it keeps its own spend within every year's budget
no start left to it keeps its crews (needed in every year of work) within its program's crews
the least that the required projects must spend in that year exceeds its budget
two or more required projects share a group
the capex of every project in the region that is not forced out is below its floor

blocks.text: The first three come per required project, in id order; then years in order, groups and regions sorted. A required project's least spend in a year is the minimum over the starts left to it. The budgets and crews in force are the snapshot's, replaced by the scenario's where it sets them; `starts`, `spend`, `budgets` and `crews` are given.

cases.says: a clean Budget Lock scenario and one that has a plan get no finding, and each of the six rules fires on its own planted error
a project planners forced in is required like a must-do, so its crews are checked
a fixed start leaves the project only that year, so a budget that fits another year no longer saves it
a project needs its crews in every year of its work, not only in its start year
a project taken out of the plan cannot help its region reach its floor
a required project that is forced out, or fixed outside its window, stays required, so the checks can report it

origin.section: Pre-Solve Checks Run First and Catch What One Limit Can Refuse

concepts: pre-solve checks that each compare one required project, group or region with one limit, and never refuse a scenario that has a plan
